options.label: A
options.textMd: Direct examination reveals the date each seed entered the soil.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Every species found later must have been dormant locally.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Species with short-lived seeds are always absent during drought.

options.label: D
options.textMd: A viable seed necessarily becomes a reproducing plant.

options.label: E
options.textMd: A species absent from one above-ground census may still contribute to later vegetation without recolonizing from elsewhere.

explanationMd: Viable local seeds provide a possible internal source of later plants. This undermines a necessary-recolonization inference without showing that every later plant came from the seed bank.

distractorRationale.c: Seed longevity alone does not imply that universal outcome.
distractorRationale.b: External recolonization is not ruled out for every species.
distractorRationale.d: The final paragraph explicitly rejects that guarantee.
